headings: Regulation by the U.S. Department of Transportation
paragraphs: Southwest Airlines Co. (the "Company" or "Southwest") operates Southwest Airlines, a major passenger airline that provides scheduled air transportation in the United States and near-international markets. Southwest commenced service on June 18, 1971, with three Boeing 737 aircraft serving three Texas cities: Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio. Southwest's unique route network, competitive fares, and famous Hospitality continue to make the Company an attractive choice for Customers in cities across the United States and near-international destinations. As of December 31, 2025, Southwest had a total of 803 Boeing 737 aircraft in its fleet and served 117 destinations in 42 states, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and ten near-international countries: Mexico, Jamaica, The Bahamas, Aruba, Dominican Republic, Costa Rica, Belize, Cuba, the Cayman Islands, and Turks and Caicos.

As part of the Company's ongoing modernization efforts, the Company is executing several transformational initiatives designed to elevate the Customer Experience on its flights, improve financial performance, and drive Shareholder value, including:

•Assigned and Extra Legroom Seating: On January 27, 2026, Southwest began operating assigned and extra legroom seating to better align with airline passenger preferences. Passengers can now choose between a standard seat, a preferred seat near the front of the cabin, or an extra legroom seat with additional pitch.

•Redesigned Boarding Model: Southwest evolved its boarding process beginning January 27, 2026, by prioritizing Customers into boarding groups based on seat location, fare bundle, and loyalty program status, beginning with extra legroom seats in boarding groups 1 and 2.

•Global Airline Partnerships: In 2025, Southwest launched its first partnerships with international carriers to expand its network and connect Customers with more global destinations to generate additional demand for travel across the Southwest network.

•Getaways by Southwest™: Southwest launched a new in-house vacation product, Getaways by Southwest ("Getaways"), in August 2025 to offer customizable vacation packages that come with Customer-friendly policies including a generous cancellation policy and flexibility with no change fees.

•24-Hour Operations: In 2025, Southwest added 24-hour operation capabilities with the introduction of overnight (i.e., redeye) flights in key markets to maximize aircraft utilization. The Company intends to expand redeye flights to additional markets in 2026.

•Marketing & Distribution Evolution: In order to attract new Customers and reach them where they are performing travel searches today, Southwest expanded into new channels such as Expedia, Priceline, Google Flights, Kayak, and Skyscanner to broaden its Customer base and begin to engage them in its loyalty program.

Southwest primarily provides "point-to-point" service, rather than the "hub-and-spoke" service provided by most major U.S. airlines. A point-to-point system enables airlines to connect directly to destinations without providing connecting service. By contrast, the hub-and-spoke system concentrates most of an airline's operations at a limited number of central hub cities and serves most other destinations in the system by providing one-stop or connecting service through a hub. By not concentrating operations exclusively through one or more central transfer points,

Southwest's route structure has allowed for more direct nonstop routing than a traditional hub-and-spoke service. To provide greater connectivity and support operational reliability and recoverability, in recent years the Company has increasingly focused on designing its network around core stations. By blending intentional connectivity offered by hub-and-spoke models and point-to-point nonstops, the Company is able to capture nonstop demand and provide reliable one-stop itinerary options.

Southwest's unique route network has also enabled it to provide its markets with frequent, conveniently timed flights and competitive fares. For example, Southwest offers up to 12 weekday roundtrips between Dallas Love Field and Houston Hobby, 12 weekday roundtrips between Sacramento and San Diego, 12 weekday roundtrips between San Diego and San Jose, 12 weekday round trips between Las Vegas and San Diego, and 11 weekday roundtrips between Las Vegas and Sacramento. Southwest complements its high-frequency short-haul routes with mid-range and long-haul nonstop service, including flights between Hawaii and California, Las Vegas, and Phoenix, and between markets such as Las Vegas and Washington Reagan, Los Angeles and Nashville, New York LaGuardia and Houston, Los Angeles and Baltimore, Oakland and Houston, and San Diego and Baltimore. As the domestic travel market has matured and structural changes have reduced the demand for short-haul travel, the Company has increased its proportion of longer-haul flights. Further, the Company introduced 24-hour operation capabilities in 2025 with the commencement of redeye flights. Southwest now offers over 50 peak-day redeye flights during peak periods and includes flights across the continental United States and from Hawaii to the U.S. mainland, with plans to offer flights from Alaska to the U.S. mainland in 2026.

headings: Information Technology, Cybersecurity, and Data Privacy Risks
Legal, Regulatory, Compliance, and Reputational Risks
Increases in insurance costs or reductions in insurance coverage may adversely impact the Company's operations and financial results.
The Company's business, operating results, and financial condition could be adversely impacted if it is unable to effectively execute its strategic plans.
The airline industry is intensely competitive.
Introducing a new aircraft manufacturer or fleet type could impose significant operational complexities, regulatory requirements, and costs on the Company.
Interruptions or disruptions in service at one of the Company's core stations have had, and could in the future have, a material adverse impact on its operations.

The airline industry is made up of inherently complex systems and is affected by many conditions that are beyond its control, which can impact the Company's business strategies and results of operations.
paragraphs: The Company's operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including but not limited to those described below. Other risks are described in "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," "Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk," and the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes thereto. The Company's business could also be affected by additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to the Company or that it currently deems to be immaterial. If any of these risks actually occurs, it could materially harm the Company's business, financial condition, or results of operations, or impair the Company's ability to implement its strategic plans. In that case, the market price of the Company's common stock could decline. The following risk factors are summarized as financial; operational; information technology, cybersecurity, and data privacy; and legal, regulatory, compliance, and reputational.

•The airline industry is particularly sensitive to changes in economic conditions, and continued or future unfavorable economic conditions or economic uncertainty could negatively affect the Company's results of operations and require the Company to adjust its business strategies.

•The Company's business, strategic plans, and profitability can be significantly affected by the availability of jet fuel, fuel prices, and volatility of fuel prices, and the Company's operations are subject to disruption in the event of any delayed supply of fuel.
•The Company's low-cost structure has historically been a competitive advantage, and many factors have and could continue to adversely affect the Company's ability to control its costs.
•Increases in insurance costs or reductions in insurance coverage may adversely impact the Company's operations and financial results.
•The Company's business, operating results, and financial condition could be adversely impacted if it is unable to effectively execute its strategic plans.

paragraphs: The Company had a record full year revenue performance in 2025, producing operating revenues of $28.1 billion, due in part to continued strong domestic travel demand, as well as the execution of transformational initiatives, which has resulted in strong financial performance and driven incremental Shareholder value.

The Company recorded results for 2025 and 2024, on an accounting principles generally accepted in the United States ("GAAP") and non-GAAP basis, as noted in the following tables. See Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures and the Reconciliation of Reported Amounts to Non-GAAP Financial Measures for additional detail regarding non-GAAP financial measures.

The Company's operating income, as shown above on a GAAP and non-GAAP basis for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased compared to the same prior year period primarily driven by revenue initiatives, including the Company's policy change related to certain Customers' first and second checked bags that became effective May 28, 2025. This increase was combined with outperformance of cost reduction goals and lower year-over-year Fuel and oil expense primarily driven by lower jet fuel prices, partially offset by higher salaries, wages, and benefits expense. Despite the negative impacts to bookings and travel associated with the government shutdown during a portion of fourth quarter 2025, the Company earned an outsized portion of its 2025 operating income during the period. On a GAAP basis, the Company achieved in excess of 90 percent, and on a non-GAAP basis, achieved in excess of 70 percent, of its annual operating income during the fourth quarter of the year, both primarily as a result of the ramp-up of its transformational and revenue initiatives over the course of the year. The Company's net income, as shown above on a GAAP and non-GAAP basis for the year ended December 31, 2025, decreased compared to the same prior year period primarily due to a decrease in interest income driven by a lower cash and investment balance. Additionally, on a GAAP basis, the Company's results for the year ended December 31, 2024, included a reversal of $116 million of breakage revenue recorded in prior years related to a portion of flight credits issued to Customers during 2022 and prior that either were redeemed or are expected to be redeemed in future periods. The majority of these flight credits were issued during the COVID-19 pandemic as the Company was making significant changes to its flight schedules based on fluctuating demand. This adjustment was treated as a special item and excluded from the Company's presentation of non-GAAP results. See Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures and the Reconciliation of Reported Amounts to Non-GAAP Financial Measures for additional detail regarding non-GAAP financial measures.

headings: 經濟與消費者保護法規
paragraphs: Southwest Airlines Co. (the "Company" or "Southwest")經營Southwest Airlines，為美國及近國際市場提供定期航空運輸服務的主要乘客航空公司。Southwest於1971年6月18日開始營運，初期以三架Boeing 737飛機服務德克薩斯州的三個城市：達拉斯、休士頓與聖安東尼奧。Southwest獨特的航線網路、競爭性票價與著名的Hospitality持續使本公司成為美國各城市與近國際目的地旅客的優選選擇。截至2025年12月31日，Southwest機隊總共有803架Boeing 737飛機，並服務42個州、華盛頓特區、波多黎各邦聯與十個近國際國家：墨西哥、牙買加、巴哈馬、阿魯巴、多明尼加共和國、哥斯達黎加、伯利茲、古巴、開曼羣島與特克斯與凱科斯羣島共計117個目的地。
為持續推動本公司現代化進程，本公司執行多項變革性計畫，旨在提升航班上的旅客體驗、改善財務表現並推動股東價值，包括：
•指定座位與額外腿部空間座位：Southwest於2026年1月27日開始運營指定座位與額外腿部空間座位，以更符合旅客偏好。旅客現在可選擇標準座位、靠近機艙前段的優先座位，或提供額外腿部空間的座位。
•重新設計的登機模式：Southwest於2026年1月27日開始優先根據座位位置、票價組合與忠誠度計畫狀態將旅客分為登機羣組，首先於登機羣組1與2提供額外腿部空間座位。
•全球航空公司合作夥伴關係：在2025年，Southwest啟動與國際電信業者的第一個合作夥伴關係，以擴展其網路並連接旅客至更多全球目的地，以產生更多跨Southwest網路的旅行需求。
•Getaways by Southwest™：Southwest於2025年8月推出內製的度假產品Getaways by Southwest（"Getaways"），提供可客製化的度假套裝，包含旅客友善的政策，包括寬鬆的取消政策與無變更費用的靈活性。
•24小時運營：在2025年，Southwest引入夜間（即紅眼航班）飛行，以在關鍵市場實現24小時運營能力，最大化飛機使用率。本公司計畫於2026年將紅眼航班擴展至更多市場。
•行銷與分銷進化：為吸引新旅客並在旅客進行旅遊搜尋的平台接觸他們，Southwest擴展至Expedia、Priceline、Google Flights、Kayak與Skyscanner等新渠道，以擴大其旅客基礎並開始在忠誠度計畫中與他們互動。

Southwest 主要提供 "point-to-point" 服務，而非大多數美國主要航空公司提供的 "hub-and-spoke" 服務。point-to-point 系統讓航空公司能直接連接到目的地，而不提供轉機服務。相較之下，hub-and-spoke 系統將航空公司大多數運作集中於有限數量的中央 hub 城市，並透過 hub 提供一站購票或轉機服務來服務其他大多數目的地。透過不 exclusively 透過一個或多個中央轉運點集中運作，
Southwest 的路線結構使其能提供比傳統 hub-and-spoke 服務更多的直接非轉機路線。為提供更佳的連通性並支撐運營可靠性與恢復力，近年來本公司 increasingly 聚焦於設計其網路圍繞核心站點。透過融合 hub-and-spoke 模型所提供的有意圖連通性與 point-to-point 非轉機服務，本公司能捕獲非轉機需求並提供可靠的單程行程選項。

Southwest 獨特的路線網路也使其能為其市場提供頻繁且時段方便的航班與具有競爭力的票價。例如，Southwest 提供最多 12 個工作日往返航班於 Dallas Love Field 與 Houston Hobby 之間，12 個工作日往返航班於 Sacramento 與 San Diego 之間，12 個工作日往返航班於 San Diego 與 San Jose 之間，12 個工作日往返航班於 Las Vegas 與 San Diego 之間，以及 11 個工作日往返航班於 Las Vegas 與 Sacramento 之間。Southwest 以高頻短程路線為基礎，搭配中程與長程非轉機服務，包括於夏威夷與加州、Las Vegas、Phoenix 之間的航班，以及於 Las Vegas 與 Washington Reagan、Los Angeles 與 Nashville、New York LaGuardia 與 Houston、Los Angeles 與 Baltimore、Oakland 與 Houston、以及 San Diego 與 Baltimore 之間的航班。隨著國內旅遊市場成熟及結構性變動減少短程旅遊需求，本公司已提高長程航班的比例。此外，本公司於 2025 年開始執行 redeye 航班，引入 24 小時運作能力。Southwest 現在於高峯時期提供超過 50 班高峯日 redeye 航班，並包含美國大陸各處及從夏威夷至美國本土的航班，並計畫於 2026 年提供從阿拉斯加至美國本土的航班。

paragraphs: 本公司在2025年創下歷史最佳的全年營業收入表現，營業收入達281億美元，部分歸因於持續強勁的國內旅遊需求，以及執行轉型性計畫，導致強勁的財務表現，並推動股東價值的增加。
本公司依美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）及非GAAP基礎，分別記載2025年及2024年的結果，如後述表格所示。有關非GAAP財務指標的使用說明及報告金額與非GAAP財務指標的對應關係，請參閱「非GAAP財務指標使用說明」及「報告金額與非GAAP財務指標對應關係」。

本公司2025年12月31日財年營運收入，依GAAP及非GAAP基礎計算，較前一財年同期增加，主要因收入計畫的執行，包括本公司針對部分客戶首、二件託運行李的政策變更，該變更自2025年5月28日起生效。此增加與成本削減目標的表現優於預期，以及較低的年對年航油費用（主要因航油價格較低）相結合，部分抵銷因較高薪資、工資及福利費用所造成的影響。儘管2025年第四季因政府停擺對預訂及旅遊造成負面影響，本公司仍於該期間取得其2025年營運收入的相當大比例。依GAAP基礎計算，本公司於該年度第四季取得超過90％的年度營運收入；依非GAAP基礎計算，則取得超過70％的年度營運收入，兩者皆因該年度內轉型性及收入計畫的逐步推進所致。本公司2025年12月31日財年淨收入，依GAAP及非GAAP基礎計算，較前一財年同期減少，主要因現金及投資餘額減少所導致的利息收入減少。此外，依GAAP基礎計算，本公司2024年12月31日財年結果包含對前年度所記錄的部分航班信用額收入1.16億美元的調整，該調整與2022年及之前期間發放給客戶的航班信用額有關，這些信用額已兌現或預期將兌現。這些航班信用額多數是在COVID-19疫情期間發放，當時本公司因應需求波動而大幅調整航班排程。此調整被視為特殊項目，並未包含在本公司非GAAP結果的呈現中。有關非GAAP財務指標的使用說明及報告金額與非GAAP財務指標的對應關係，請參閱「非GAAP財務指標使用說明」及「報告金額與非GAAP財務指標對應關係」。

paragraphs: 本公司之營運及財務表現受多種風險與不確定性影響，包括但不限於下列所列風險。其他風險於『項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析』、『項目 7A. 市場風險之量化與質化揭露』及合併財務報表及其相關附註中有所說明。本公司之業務亦可能受其他目前尚未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性影響。若上述任何風險實際發生，可能會對本公司之業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大損害，或影響本公司執行其戰略計畫之能力。在此情況下，本公司普通股之市價可能下跌。以下風險因素歸納為財務；營運；資訊科技、網路安全與資料隱私；以及法律、法規、合規與聲譽等類別。
•航空業對經濟條件之變動特別敏感，持續或未來不利之經濟條件或經濟不確定性可能對本公司之營運結果造成負面影響，並可能迫使本公司調整其業務策略。

•本公司之低成本結構歷來為競爭優勢，許多因素已且可能繼續對本公司控制成本之能力造成不利影響。
